b: A locust plague becomes the lens for a warning about judgment and a promise of restoration. Peter quotes chapter 2 at Pentecost to explain what has just happened.

2.t: And not your garments. Return to the LORD, for he is gracious and compassionate — quoting Exodus 34.

2.h: I will pour out my Spirit
2.t: On all flesh — sons, daughters, old, young, male and female servants. Peter quotes it at Pentecost to explain what has happened.

1.t: Four waves, each finishing what the last left. Joel makes a natural disaster the occasion for national repentance.

3.t: A deliberate reversal of Isaiah 2, addressed to the nations rather than to Israel.
